name: Haguro-san stone steps, Dewa Sanzan (羽黒山)
why: The pilgrims' way of the yamabushi: 2,446 stone steps under giant cedars, past a thousand-year-old cedar and a wooden pagoda, to the great thatched shrine of the three holy mountains.
book: Free, no permit. Buses from Tsuruoka station to Zuishinmon (Haguro centre) and on to the summit car park: walk up and ride down, or the reverse. The Ideha Bunka Museum by the gate lends sneakers, rubber boots and sticks for free (closed Tuesdays).
water: A tea house on the Ni-no-saka slope, halfway up; drinks, toilets and food at the summit. Carry 0.5-1 litre.
dangers: The stone steps are mossy and very slippery when wet: no sandals or smooth soles.
Snow on the steps from December to March.
Hornets and horseflies in late summer.
turnaround: Too tired at the pagoda? Go back down the 15 minutes to the gate; or keep going and take the bus down from the summit.

points.name: Zuishinmon gate
points.note: The red gate where the pilgrims' way begins; the path drops down the Mamakozaka slope to the Harai river and the Suga waterfall.

points.name: Haguro five-storey pagoda
points.note: A 29 m wooden pagoda alone among cedars, said to date from 938, a National Treasure, just past the Jijisugi cedar, over 1,000 years old. The steps begin after it.

points.name: Haguro summit shrine
points.note: Sanjin Gosaiden, 414 m: one thick thatched roof over the gods of all three mountains, with a lotus pond in front. Buses leave from the car park behind.
